mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in RETAIL_REC mobility, coupled with sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicates a prevailing public caution or reduced discretionary spending that will continue to depress retail activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the recent downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility, as observed in the latest data, suggests a reduction in office attendance and associated weekday retail traffic, leading to a further decline in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite the significant drop in WORKPLACES mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility and GROCERY_PHARM visits indicates a shift towards essential outings and staying home, reducing non-essential retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows an upward trend over the next 28 days, despite sustained high RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The continued decline in TRANSIT station visits, reaching a new low in the latest week, suggests ongoing or new public health advisories discouraging non-essential travel, which will suppress RETAIL_REC mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while TRANSIT mobility remains at or below current levels.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in PARKS mobility, indicating reduced outdoor leisure activities, often precedes a broader reduction in discretionary out-of-home activities, thus predicting a further decrease in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days, despite the recent decline in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and significant drops in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggest a widespread reduction in daily commuting and associated activities, which will directly translate to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows an increase over the next 28 days, despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining low or declining further.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and strong upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates a focus on essential errands, which often correlates with reduced discretionary spending and out-of-home activities, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility, particularly if it exceeds 10% change from baseline in the current week and one of the previous two weeks, implies continued encouragement or mandates for staying home, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility is above 10% in the current week and was above 10% in one of the previous two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining high.
